steps: Hold your dominant hand in an upright U handshape, with the index and middle fingers extended together.
Keep your non-dominant hand flat and steady at chest height, palm facing downward.
Brush the wrist of the dominant U hand twice across the top of the non-dominant hand, like dusting a surface.
Angle the dominant palm slightly sideways so the U points backward as it slides across the base hand.
Keep your face neutral — the double brushing motion is part of the sign, not added emphasis.
tip: It shares the sign for USE — the two brush strokes mark the thing as worth using.

steps: Form an R handshape with your dominant hand by crossing the middle finger over the index finger.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat and upright at chest height, its palm facing toward your dominant hand.
Touch the dominant palm to the base palm, lift off slightly, slide down an inch, and touch the base palm again.
Keep the dominant palm facing the base palm through both contacts of the sign.
Hold a neutral, serious expression — this sign carries the weight of an official regulation.
tip: Same motion as LAW with an R hand — swap back to an L handshape and it reads as LAW instead.

steps: Shape both hands into loose 5 handshapes with the fingers spread and slightly bent.
Hold both hands up at chest height in front of your body, palms facing each other.
Point the fingertips of each hand toward the fingertips of the other hand, picturing lanes of cars.
Move the hands back and forth past each other in small alternating motions, like vehicles streaming in opposite lanes.
Keep the palms facing each other through the whole alternating movement.
Hold a matter-of-fact expression — the sign simply names the condition of traffic.
tip: The bent fingers are the lanes, not the cars — hands passing each other picture a busy multi-lane road.
